description: NX Warp test corpus. See corpus/README.md for the schema and corpus/fetch.py to materialise it. Files live under $NXW_CORPUS, never in this repository. Entries whose generator block says legacy:true are version 1 material kept for reproducibility; the -v2 entries are the band-limited replacements (tools/quality/reports/gates-v2-2026-09-04.md).

classes.synthetic-vr: Rendered stereo views out of a procedural equirectangular panorama with a scripted head pose. Geometrically exact for the rotation-only reprojection of PAPER 2.2, so a warp failure here is the codec's, not the material's.
classes.text-panel: Quad-layer content: text at two scales, hard edges, static for seconds. The 4:2:0 chroma-fringe case; PAPER 5.2 locks text to lossless.
classes.head-rotation: Sequences whose pose log spans a wide range of angular velocity, so PAPER 2.11 item 1's split at the 20 percent highest-velocity frames is computable.
classes.stereo-pair: Side-by-side stereo with real disparity from near-field geometry. Material for the Phase 4 inter-view tools.
classes.natural: Public camera-captured sequences. Not VR material, but the coding-tool sanity check every codec is expected to survive, and the only content class with decades of published anchors.
classes.wivrn-capture: Real frames and pose logs grabbed from a WiVRn NX session (tools/quality/README.md 1c). The material the Phase 1 and Phase 2 gates are actually stated on.

entries.name: vr-static-256
entries.note: At-rest coding. The denominator for every 'better on motion frames' claim. LEGACY (version 1 material): the generator point-sampled its panorama once per output sample at 2.1x the eye's angular resolution, so these frames carry pose-independent aliasing worth 7.2 dB full-frame / 14.4 dB centre on the ideal-warp ceiling (docs/WARP-AUDIT.md section 4). Kept, pinned and reproducible -- gen_synthetic.py --legacy regenerates it bit for bit -- so that every number published on it stays checkable. New measurements use the -v2 entry of the same name.

entries.name: vr-static-256-v2
entries.note: At-rest coding. The denominator for every 'better on motion frames' claim. Band-limited v2 material: panorama at 16x the eye width (4.2x its angular resolution) with features sized in eye pixels, a latitude-aware longitudinal prefilter, and 4x4 box supersampling of the render. The pose log carries the measured ideal-warp PSNR ceiling, which is what every RD number on it should be read against.

entries.name: panel-static-256
entries.note: No moving objects, no head-locked HUD: what is left is the panorama's own text panels, checkerboards and colour bars against a still camera. Encode this in 4:2:0 and 4:4:4 and compare the text: the difference is the chroma-fringe case PAPER 5.2 answers with lossless quad layers. LEGACY (version 1 material): the generator point-sampled its panorama once per output sample at 2.1x the eye's angular resolution, so these frames carry pose-independent aliasing worth 7.2 dB full-frame / 14.4 dB centre on the ideal-warp ceiling (docs/WARP-AUDIT.md section 4). entries.name: xiph-foreman-cif
entries.license: Long-standing free research test sequence redistributed by Xiph.org; no explicit licence file is published alongside it. Do not redistribute; use for evaluation.
entries.note: The oldest sanity check there is: head-and-shoulders with camera pan and a background that punishes bad motion handling. In .y4m, so it needs one ffmpeg pass to raw planar (see corpus/README.md).

entries.name: xiph-mobile-cif
entries.license: Long-standing free research test sequence redistributed by Xiph.org; no explicit licence file. Do not redistribute; use for evaluation.
entries.note: High spatial detail and slow global motion: the classic 'does your transform actually work' clip, and the one where a resampling-blur regression is unmissable.

entries.name: xiph-park-joy-1080p50
entries.source: SVT High Definition Multi Format test set, redistributed by Xiph.org (derf)
entries.license: Sveriges Television AB released this set for research use, copyright retained. Not redistributable; download it yourself.
entries.note: About 1.5 GB, so far above the default --max-mb cap that --download will refuse it until you raise the cap deliberately. Worth the disk once: it is high-motion 1080p50 with published anchors, which makes it the cheapest external cross-check that our BD-rate machinery agrees with the literature.

entries.name: wivrn-vrchat-1440
entries.source: WiVRn NX session, encoder: raw + WIVRN_DUMP_VIDEO (tools/quality/README.md 1c)
entries.license: Private capture. Never commit, never publish: it is a recording of someone's session.
entries.note: NOT YET RECORDED. The social-VR case of PAPER 5.5: dozens of animated avatars, particles, mirrors -- the content class expected to set the bitrate floor. Recording it needs foveation degenerated to identity, FSR1 and motion smoothing off, per the caveats in the harness README.

entries.name: wivrn-beatsaber-1440
entries.source: WiVRn NX session, encoder: raw + WIVRN_DUMP_VIDEO
entries.license: Private capture. Never commit, never publish.
entries.note: NOT YET RECORDED. Fast sustained head motion with a mostly static world: the best case for pose-warped prediction, and one of the three 60 s recordings PAPER 2.11 item 1 names as the parity kill test.

entries.name: wivrn-alyx-1440
entries.source: WiVRn NX session, encoder: raw + WIVRN_DUMP_VIDEO
entries.license: Private capture. Never commit, never publish.
entries.note: NOT YET RECORDED. The third of PAPER 2.11 item 1's recordings: near-field hands at large parallax, which is exactly the case the coarse +-16 px MV search may miss (item 5).
